title: Signature 40% Chocolate Chip Cookies 400g $4 (Was $5) @ ALDI
body:
Deal: Signature 40% Chocolate Chip Cookies 400g $4 (Was $5) @ ALDI

[tunzafun001] I literally just stumbled across a pack.
They aren't as good as the Coles ones from 2 years ago (last time I bought them).
They are harder/ crispy mouth feel. The Coles version was softer/ smoother..
[dosada] Funny how only a German based company manages to lower the prices while the locals rip us still off.
[cheapaschips] Woolworths cookies are $2.80? Even cheaper than this.(albeit not the same tasting)
Or are people comparing Aldis home brand against a Woolworths/coles branded product again(like Arnotts)?
When you compare both own brand products(which Aldi rip off to look like popular brands and fools people) , Woolworths/Coles are usually same if not cheaper
Dont be fooled by marketing by Aldi.
[flumpf] Better dan Coles. Better dan others. Best cookie! OM NOM NOM!!!
[WavyClock] Just bought it a couple of hours ago, got back home and in the ingredient list it says 29% dark choc chips. Have bought it a few times before and they were great. But did it always say 29% on the back? Or is this discount really a reduction in choc chips (front packaging not updated)?
Can't really tell by looking at the cookies. Last time I bought it was a few months ago
[Benno123] It's 29% dark chocolate chips and 11% milk chocolate chips for 40% total. I think that's always been the case
[WavyClock] Oh you are right, my eyes just skipped over the milk choc chips
[dealBuoy] It says in the ingredients list Palm Oil under Vegetable Oil. Don’t be fooled by the “real butter” Marketting!
[tenpercent] I don't think anyone would mistake vegetable oil for butter. Besides it says "Includes Palm Oil" so it may include other vegetable oil too.
This is the bit that is real butter:
Butter (Milk) (4%)
[batrarobin] Good call out. Really hard to find biscuits or cookies these days that have no palm oil.
